title: Para-aminosalicylic acid
dek: 1940s folate-pathway salvage. GI intolerance, hypothyroidism with ETH, thyA/folC/dfrA genetics. Not Group A. See also the folate plate.
story: PAS was among the first TB chemotherapies. It remains a Group C option when shorter all-oral regimens fail or are ineligible. Adult doses are large (grams of PAS-sodium), GI toxicity is legendary, and hypothyroidism is common when paired with ethionamide.
Mechanism: folate/thymidylate poisoning (see tb-folate-salvage). Resistance: thyA, folC, dfrA, ribD — scattered, catalogue-incomplete. Do not regex a synonymous folC lineage SNP into PAS-R.
Never a BPaLM component. Never TPT. If you need PAS, you should also be talking about surgery, trials, and whether any Group A residual remains.
deep: Granules vs tablets vs sodium salt change GI and PK. Use the product your NTP stocks.
TSH if combined with ETH. Electrolytes with some PAS-sodium loads.
Cotrimoxazole is not a PAS substitute for TB, even in HIV.

visual.caption: PAS as last-shelf folate salvage. Genetics exist; so does a GI wall that stops the drug before the allele does.
